raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
# What does this PR do ?

`StateDict` membership checks scanned the full key list on every call, so per-key loops during HF import (`state[k]`, `k in state`) were quadratic in the number of checkpoint keys. This switches them to set lookups.

# Changelog

- `StateDict._get_key_set()`: a set over `source.get_all_keys()`, used by `__getitem__`, `__contains__`, `get`, list access and exact-key `_match_keys`. Both in-tree sources return a cached list, so the set is built once; it is rebuilt only when the source hands back a different list (the Kimi K2.5-VL / K3 bridges temporarily wrap `get_all_keys` with virtual keys during `build_conversion_tasks`).
- `SafeTensorsStateSource.load_tensors`: cache each shard's key set next to its reused `safe_open` handle instead of rebuilding `set(f.keys())` per call. Dropped together with the handle in `_invalidate_handle`, so the retry path still re-reads a replaced shard (covered by the existing `test_retry_refreshes_incomplete_shard`).
- Test: `test_membership_follows_wrapped_get_all_keys` checks membership before, during and after wrapping `get_all_keys`. Passes on main, fails on a build-once cache, passes here.

# Benchmark

Synthetic checkpoints with real key names and one-element tensors, so this measures lookup overhead only, not end-to-end import time. CPU, `StateDict(SafeTensorsStateSource(path))`, keys warmed first.

| Checkpoint shape | Keys / shards | per-key `state[k]` loop | `k in state` loop |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V3 | 94,370 / 163 | 223.2s -> 12.6s | 106.5s -> 0.07s |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B | 73,229 / 118 | 110.8s -> 9.0s | 58.8s -> 0.04s |

# Tests

`uv run python -m pytest tests/unit_tests/models/hf_pretrained/`: 193 passed, on this branch and with main's `state.py` (same tests, including the new one). Also `tests/unit_tests/models/kimi_vl/test_kimi_k25_vl_bridge.py`: 24 passed. Run on a CPU-only box: CPU torch wheel, Megatron-LM submodule installed editable, and `transformer_engine` replaced by a local import stub so `megatron.bridge` imports without CUDA. pre-commit passes on the changed files.

# Additional Information

AI disclosure: I used Claude Code to profile this and write the change; I reviewed the diff, tests and benchmark.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

@@ -196,13 +196,26 @@ def __init__(self, source: Dict[str, torch.Tensor] | "StateSource"):

+        self._key_set: set[str] | None = None
+        self._key_set_source: List[str] | None = None
 
     def _get_all_keys(self) -> List[str]:
         """
         Get all available tensor keys from the underlying source.
         """
         return self.source.get_all_keys()
 
+    def _get_key_set(self) -> set[str]:
+        # Membership checks run once per tensor during conversion; a list scan made
+        # them quadratic in the number of checkpoint keys. Sources return a cached
+        # list, so the set is rebuilt only if they hand back a different one (e.g.
+        # while a bridge temporarily wraps ``get_all_keys`` with virtual keys).
+        keys = self._get_all_keys()
+        if self._key_set_source is not keys:
+            self._key_set = set(keys)
+            self._key_set_source = keys
+        return self._key_set
+
     def _load_tensors(self, keys_to_load: List[str]) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
         """

+    def test_membership_follows_wrapped_get_all_keys(self, mock_model):
